title: Local Batuta event (~/.batuta/events.jsonl)
description: LOCAL FORMAT. NEVER UPLOADED. This is the file that lives at ~/.batuta/events.jsonl, one JSON line per event, and it has no destination address: no Batuta command sends a raw event anywhere, even with opt-in enabled. What gets uploaded is exclusively the aggregate from schema/daily-summary.schema.json. It is documented here because the format is public and auditable — whoever installs Batuta has the right to read, field by field, what the tool writes on their own machine. Practical consequence: the portal's ingestion endpoint rejects, with 400, any body that contains the keys 'prompt', 'prompt_hash', 'turn' or 'text' at any level — if a raw event got there, it's a client bug, not new data. Generated by crates/batuta/src/route.rs (type 'route') and crates/batuta/src/main.rs, cmd_log (types 'activation' and 'outcome').

turn.description: Ties together the three signals of the same turn (§4.4). Router default: prompt_hash[..12] — hence it's local data and is not uploaded.

prompt_hash.description: sha256(local_salt || prompt)[..32]. The salt never leaves the machine, so not even the file's owner can test a prompt guess against another machine's hash. Even so: this field is not uploaded.

prompt_len.description: Length in characters. Size, not content.

holdout.description: Turn randomly selected for the router to stay silent. Deterministic draw from salt + prompt: the same question always lands in the same arm, so there's no way to retry until the router speaks.

mode.description: Transport (§4.1). 'mcp' and 'skill' are incomplete funnels and become 'degraded' in the aggregate.

suggestions.description: Empty when the router stayed silent — due to holdout or no match above the noise cutoff (2.0). Silence is a result, not a failure.

score.description: BM25 score (K1=1.5, B=0.75), rounded to 2 decimal places.

by.description: Who triggered it. Kept separate because a skill that only fires when the user commands it wasn't routed — it was requested.

outcome.title: outcome — did this turn end well?

ok.description: Absence of both --ok and --failed records false: when in doubt, the turn doesn't count as a success.

turns.description: Turns until the task ends. Becomes the aggregate's median.

source.description: Who said it ended well: 'proxy' (reprompt/error/retry, hard and cheap), 'vote' (one keypress from the user) or 'judge' (nightly batch, blind and versioned). Judge is a signal, never the sole truth.
